headline: Acton Street two-way request held; Ward Street school no-parking and Oak Ave driveway no-parking approved.
summary: The committee approved many handicap parking, no-parking, stop sign, and crosswalk requests. It held the Acton Street two-way request and several others for more study or amended wording. It filed other requests, some because staff said they did not meet traffic warrants or were already in place.
decisions: Approved a handicap parking space at 49 Whipple Street, 3-0.
Filed the request for a handicap parking space at 50 Bristol Street.
Held the request to remove the handicap space at 54 Ward Street so it can be readvertised for the correct space number.
Held the request for two handicap spaces at 243 Tacoma Street, 3-0.
Approved no parking on the even side of South Street between Providence Street and Chapin Street, 3-0.
Approved no parking on Ward Street between Richland Street and Dorchester Street, 7 to 8 a.m. and 2 to 3 p.m., Monday through Friday, 3-0.
Approved a No Parking Here to Corner sign at Rodney Street and Catherine Street, 3-0.
Held the request for no parking across from the driveways at 48 Winham Street so the wording can be amended.
Approved no parking signs near the driveways at 41 and 45 Oak Ave, 3-0.
Approved no parking 20 feet from the Whipple Street intersection on Blackstone River Road, 3-0.
Held the requests for no parking on the north side of Acton Street and removal of its one-way designation, 3-0, for further study.
Filed the request for four-way stop signs at West Street and William Street by a 2-1 vote; the chair ordered no parking signs within 20 feet of the intersection.
Filed the request for three-way stop signs at Valleyhill Drive and Valleyhill Lane, 3-0; the chair ordered traffic-calming measures.
Approved a stop sign on Warton Street at Englewood Avenue, 3-0.
Filed the request for a stop sign on Clive Street at Mentor Street, 3-0.
Filed the request for a stop sign at Englewood Avenue and Minthorne Street; the chair ordered warning signs.
Filed the request for a stop sign at May Street and Lovell Street, because a four-way stop there was already ordained.
Approved a stop sign on Ennis Drive at Westport Road.
Filed the request for one-hour parking in front of 326 Shrewsbury Street; staff said a work order was placed to add the signs.
Approved Not a Truck Route signs at Westchester Street and Chester Street, and at Chester Street and Grove Street.
Held the request for a truck weight restriction near Shore Drive and Holden Street, so the location can be clarified.
Denied the motion to change the permanent winter parking ban on Hamilton Street to a declared ban; the chair ruled there was no majority.
Filed the Hamilton Street winter parking request, 3-0.
Approved barriers on Hamilton Street near Fairmount Avenue, with flex posts as an interim step and a chair's order for curb extensions.
Filed the request for two permanent speed monitors on Shrewsbury Street, 3-0.
Approved one permanent speed monitor on Belmont Street, eastbound, pending funding for purchase and installation.
Filed the requests for a winter parking ban change on Providence Street between Waverly Street and Winthrop Street.
Approved a crosswalk on Reactor E Drive.
Approved an ADA-compliant curb ramp on Hurst Street across from Waterman Street.
Approved a crosswalk at Massasoit Road and Miscoe Road, with a rapid flashing beacon to be added during the road redesign.
Filed the school safety zone signage request near Thorndyke Road School; the recommended changes will need ordinances.
Filed the request for traffic signal changes at Mountain Street and West Boylston Street and ordered protected left-turn phasing, pending funding.
Filed the request for fog lines on Lovell Street near Columbus Park Preparatory Academy.
Held the request for a traffic study at Clark Street, Eunice Avenue, and Bay State Road for further study.
Filed the request for traffic calming on Apthorp Street; the chair ordered speed humps added to the candidate list.
discussion: Acton Street two-way request: Discussion centered on signal timing, truck turns, and the load on a signal pole. Staff recommended a hold while those studies are done.

Apthorp Street speeding: Residents said traffic has grown and cars speed down the hill. Staff reported an average speed of 24 mph and an 85th percentile speed of 29 mph, and said speed humps and police enforcement would be considered.

Holden Street truck restriction: Residents said trucks and school buses speed on Holden Street. Staff said the street's role as a minor arterial makes a truck ban harder to approve, and the item was held.

Hamilton Street winter ban: Residents disagreed on whether the permanent ban should stay, citing parking needs and snow clearing. Staff said the ban helps crews clear the street, and the motion to change it to a declared ban failed.

South Street and Chapin Street parking: Residents said parking from nearby uses crowds the street, and a two-way section forces traffic to alternate. Staff recommended no parking only on the two-way part.
